name: Skillet Gnocchi With Miso Butter and Asparagus
desc: Ali Slagle's one-skillet shelf-stable gnocchi, seared instead of boiled, with asparagus, arugula, and a miso butter glaze.

source.title: Skillet Gnocchi With Miso Butter and Asparagus
source.evidence: Same title and author, the same 16 to 18 oz shelf-stable gnocchi, 4 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp white miso, 2 tsp vinegar, 1 lb asparagus and 2 packed cups arugula, and the same covered sear, miso butter off the heat method.

ingredients.raw: 18 oz shelf-stable potato gnocchi (do not boil)
4 tbsp unsalted butter, at room temperature
1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, plus more to taste
1 lb asparagus (1 bunch), tough ends trimmed, cut into 1-inch pieces
ingredients.prep: tough ends trimmed, cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.raw: 1/4 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste

steps: Heat the olive oil in a large nonstick or well-seasoned cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Break apart any gnocchi that are stuck together and add them in an even layer. Cover and cook, undisturbed, until golden brown underneath and releasing from the pan, 2-4 min.
While the gnocchi sear, smash the butter, miso, vinegar, and 1/4 tsp pepper together in a small bowl with a fork until fully combined.
Add the asparagus and 1/4 tsp salt to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the asparagus is bright green and crisp-tender, 2-3 min.
Turn off the heat and add the miso butter in spoonfuls. Stir until it melts and the gnocchi are glossy. Season with salt and pepper, stir in the arugula until barely wilted, and serve right away.
tips: The NYT recipe uses 1 tbsp vegetable or canola oil, sherry vinegar in the miso butter, and 1/2-inch asparagus pieces; this version uses olive oil, rice vinegar, and 1-inch pieces. Either vinegar works.
